summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments in 4.1 minutes, including 10 compute-bound experiments. Model-family factor harness development and held-split freeze was the compute timing leader at 1.39 minutes, but the supplied timing does not identify a causal phase.
bottlenecks_identified: The timing reconstruction ranks tasks but does not split gate wait, setup, model load, inference, or synthesis time, so it cannot explain why the compute leader took longest.
Three of the four compute-bound entries in the slowest list depend on prerequisite gates; the data does not separate necessary dependency time from dispatch delay.
The GPU snapshot is not correlated with task intervals, so it cannot grade GPU efficiency for the compute-bound work; the locked task classification does not identify compute-bound GPU idling.
No model-concurrency count or runner-selection receipt is available, so the data cannot determine whether any parallel multi-model task missed DualGPURunner.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic per-task phase timing for gate wait, setup, model load, inference, and synthesis.
Attach periodic GPU utilization samples to the active experiment and its compute-bound classification.
Record loaded-model concurrency and runner selection for each compute task, and require a DualGPURunner receipt only when two or more models run in parallel.
Dispatch independent gate-ready work automatically when a prerequisite completes, while preserving declared dependencies.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add task-scoped phase timing so the next retrospective can target measured execution or gate-handoff cost.
Correlate GPU samples, loaded-model count, and runner selection with each compute task.
Add event-driven dispatch for independent gate-ready work.
meta_reflection: The milestone was brief, but disk-mtime reconstruction and a point-in-time GPU snapshot do not support causal efficiency claims. The next retrospective needs task-linked phase and accelerator telemetry before it can assign a nonzero speedup estimate.
